search_log: Searched "Stephen King Fairy Tale official excerpt Charlie I narrator", "site:stephenking.com Fairy Tale excerpt", and "site:simonandschuster.com Fairy Tale Stephen King excerpt"; found and opened the authorized Simon & Schuster interior excerpt.

Searched "Fairy Tale Stephen King first person narrator point of view" and targeted review queries for "first-person narration" and "Charlie Reade"; opened explicit whole-book and interior corroboration.

Searched exact quote strings including "I don't want to be a Disney prince", "Here is something I learned in Empis", and "All alcohol smells the same to me"; results did not supply reliable surrounding prose for the locally ambiguous quotation.

Searched "Fairy Tale Stephen King alternating narration narrators", "multiple narrators", "epistolary frame narrative", and ending-narrator queries; found no credible indication of sustained narration in another grammatical person.

Opened a Pittsburgh Post-Gazette review whose search result explicitly described Charlie and the novel's first-person narration, but the opened page did not expose the article body reliably, so it was not relied upon as recorded evidence.
person_note: Charlie Reade is the controlling participating narrator, retrospectively recounting his own experiences in the first person. Multiple event quotes independently expose that voice, and the authorized Simon & Schuster interior excerpt sustains it after Charlie enters the other world; whole-book and later-scene reviews corroborate the structure. Dialogue, aphorisms, an attributed quotation, and the epigraph are local non-base material, while q06889 is merely unmarked rather than third-person evidence. The only material uncertainty is the lost local boundary around q06881, not the book-level person; targeted research found no sustained second- or third-person strand.
